title: Deactivating a part with a core charge also deactivates its core
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-CORE-01) is active at {Location-A} with a Core Charge above 0 (for example 25.00), so it has a core.
custom_steps:
1. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  2. Type {Part-A} in the Search box.
  3. Click the ⋮ actions menu button in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  4. Click Deactivate parts.
  5. Count the rows the list shows.
  6. Click the {Part-A} row.
  7. Click the Deactivate button on the bar.
  8. Click Deactivate in the "Deactivate parts?" confirmation.
  9. Click the Inactive tab.
  10. Type {Part-A} in the Search box, replacing any text there.
  11. Click the ⋮ actions menu button.
  12. Click Activate parts.
  13. Click the {Part-A} row.
  14. Click the Activate button on the bar.
  15. Click Activate in the "Activate parts?" confirmation.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 5: One row is listed, for {Part-A}. Its core has no row of its own, so the core cannot be ticked.
  • Step 8: A green toast reads "1 part updated.": only the part you ticked is counted, not its core, and no failure is listed. {Part-A} leaves the Active tab.
  • Step 8: The core becomes inactive together with {Part-A}. The core's status and history show only on the core's own Part History page, which cannot be opened from the Inventory list because the core has no row: write "core status not checked by hand" in the result comment.
  • Step 10: {Part-A} is on the Inactive tab, as one row, with no separate row for its core.
  • Step 15: A green toast reads "1 part updated." and {Part-A} leaves the Inactive tab. Its core becomes active with it (core status not checked by hand).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk); story SV-10816 (Story 3, Activate Parts in Bulk); story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S2-R17, S2-N3, S3-R3, S10-R12a, §4 Key Decisions, S5-E3, S10-R19, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 4.3 (Two rows ticked), board 4.6 (Inactive tab, Activate parts), 13 Oct copy. Product's 9 Oct answer (Chris Ward, question 9); QA lead's 9 Oct set-up answer 5 (where cores show). Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R17: “A part's core becomes inactive together with the part, in the same change.”
  • S10-R12a: “The counts include only the parts the user selected. A core that changes with its part is not counted, so changing 2 parts that both have a core reads "2 parts updated."”
  • S3-R3: “S2-R3 to S2-R10b, S2-R14 to S2-R17 and S2-N3 apply on the Inactive tab exactly as on the Active tab, with "deactivate" read as "activate". The disabled button's hover text is "Tick the parts to activate".”
  • S2-N3: “A core cannot be set active or inactive on its own. Asked to, the system refuses it with "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead."”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions (A core follows its part): “A core follows its part. A core is never activated, deactivated, tracked or untracked on its own.”
  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (A core asked to change status on its own): “"A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead." | Listed as the failure reason”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • S10-R19: “A core's status change writes its own Part History entry on the core.”
